KN-LIT-4f3b80.corrected_title: A Single-Trace Side-Channel Attack on ML-DSA: Practical Full-Key Recovery from a Single Faulty Signature
KN-LIT-4f3b80.author: Jendral

step_1_kn_lit_056_hedged_mode_claim.abstract_from_tches: In this paper, we present the lattice-based signature scheme Dilithium, which is a component of the CRYSTALS (Cryptographic Suite for Algebraic Lattices) suite that was submitted to NIST's call for post-quantum cryptographic standards. The design of the scheme avoids all uses of discrete Gaussian sampling and is easily implementable in constant-time. For the same security levels, our scheme has a public key that is 2.5X smaller than the previously most efficient lattice-based schemes that did not use Gaussians, while having essentially the same signature size.
step_1_kn_lit_056_hedged_mode_claim.justification: The TCHES 2018 abstract does not mention hedged signing mode. The hedged-mode specification and security claim would be in the paper body (a section on randomized vs. deterministic signing). Full text not accessed. Cannot determine from available abstract whether hedged-mode security is a formal theorem with reduction or an informal design argument.
caveats: Full text required for this determination; abstract does not address hedged mode

step_3_kn_lit_8ce0b5_seed_derivation.stated_fault_class: twiddle-perturbation faults on the forward NTT
step_3_kn_lit_8ce0b5_seed_derivation.justification: KN-LIT-8ce0b5 abstract confines its fault class to NTT twiddle perturbations. The hedged ML-DSA seed derivation step computes rho' = H(xi || M || rnd) using a hash function (SHAKE-256 or equivalent). This is a hash computation, not NTT arithmetic over secret-bearing polynomials. The seed derivation step is NTT-independent and therefore outside the stated scope of KN-LIT-8ce0b5.

step_4_kn_lit_4f3b80_attack_mechanism.abstract_text: CRYSTALS-Dilithium is a post-quantum secure digital signature algorithm currently being standardised by NIST. As a result, devices making use of CRYSTALS-Dilithium will soon become generally available and be deployed in various environments. It is thus important to assess the resistance of CRYSTALS-Dilithum implementations to physical attacks. In this paper, we present an attack on a CRYSTALS-Dilithium implementation in hedged mode in ARM Cortex-M4 using fault injection. Voltage glitching is performed to skip computation of a seed during the generation of the signature. We identified settings that consistently skip the desired function without crashing the device. After the successful fault injection, the resulting signature allows for the extraction of the secret key vector. Our attack succeeds with probability 0.582 in a single trace. We also propose countermeasures against the presented attack.
step_4_kn_lit_4f3b80_attack_mechanism.faulted_computation: skip computation of a seed during signature generation
step_4_kn_lit_4f3b80_attack_mechanism.seed_interpretation: The 'seed' skipped corresponds to the per-signature randomness rnd in rho' = H(xi || M || rnd). Skipping this computation effectively sets rnd = 0 or exposes xi directly.
step_4_kn_lit_4f3b80_attack_mechanism.key_extraction_mechanism: z - y = c * s_1 extraction (from faulty signature where y is deterministic from xi)
step_4_kn_lit_4f3b80_attack_mechanism.attack_applies_to_deterministic_mode: not stated in abstract; hedged mode is the targeted mode
caveats: Full text not available; z - y = c*s_1 extraction step confirmed from KN-LIT-4f3b80 KN entry but not verbatim from paper

jendral_nonce_erasure_vs_kn_lit_056.justification: Cannot determine whether KN-LIT-056 states hedged-mode security as a formal theorem or informal argument without reading the paper body. Abstract does not mention hedged mode.

jendral_nonce_erasure_vs_kn_lit_3907.justification: KN-LIT-3907 is a CMA proof. Standard CMA game uses a fault-free signing oracle. The Jendral attack requires physical hardware access to voltage-glitch the signing device. Physical fault adversaries are typically outside mathematical CMA models. However, full text is blocked; whether KN-LIT-3907 specifically addresses hedged mode or nonce-erasure adversaries cannot be confirmed.

jendral_nonce_erasure_vs_kn_lit_8ce0b5.justification: KN-LIT-8ce0b5 scope is NTT twiddle-perturbation faults. Seed derivation (rho' = H(xi || M || rnd)) is hash computation, not NTT arithmetic. The Jendral attack targets the hash computation step. Outside KN-LIT-8ce0b5's scope by omission.

ctrl_2.corpus_completeness_caveat: This gap assessment is scoped to the corpus entries KN-LIT-3907, KN-LIT-056, and KN-LIT-8ce0b5 and does not claim to survey all published formal proofs of hedged ML-DSA signing security.

ctrl_3.scheme_vs_implementation: The Jendral attack's 0.582 success probability is a hardware fault injection success rate on Cortex-M4. This is an implementation-level probability (dependent on physical device, fault injection setup, and glitch parameters). The formal proof coverage question (whether the scheme's security proof covers nonce-erasure adversaries) is a separate question from the hardware attack success rate.
ctrl_3.interpretation: The 0.582 rate is implementation-level; the formal proof coverage question is scheme-level. Both questions can be asked independently.
